## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The modbus integration has an established connection with a tcp peer. When reloading HA yaml files it terminates the connection and establishes a new connection within the same millisecond. The new connection attempt then fails from within pymodbus with errno 111, but the modbus integration keeps trying to read values after not evaluating whether the connection attempt was (un-)successful.

The PR introduces a restart_delay (default=0) after closing an existing connection and before re-creating a new connection and further evaluates and tests on the pymodbus connected property.

> If this is something that happens on all setups, would it make sense to pick a sane default and not make this configurable at all?

I'd prefer fixing my local issue first and cannot speak to 'all setups'. Making it optional for now can help affected HA users fix their setup while not touching other installs. We can raise the default value of 0 to 1 after some time has passed depending on whether new issues get filed against modbus?

> We can raise the default value of 0 to 1 after some time has passed depending on whether new issues get filed against modbus?

So personally (without any knowledge about modbus) I think it makes sense to default to 1 as having such a small delay is insignificant. I triggered the CI so please fix those issues, I hope someone familiar with modbus will chime in to review the PR.

I kinda agree with @rytilahti in this case. It might be better to just add a sane default and thus a little delay by default. Introducting more options isn't always better, it only makes things more complicated, while it should "just work"™️
@frenck @rytilahti I was updating the default sleep from 0 seconds to 1 second per your suggestion.
Right, but should it be an option even?

While 1 second can be a sane default restart delay value, having it as an option allows to:
- users to fallback to the old behavior in case they want or need.
- users to increase the delay in case they want or need.

I'm willing to remove the option but leave the decision up to someone more familiar with the code and HA in general.

You tell me, please.

I think we should remove the option; I would rather introduce options if the need for it occurs for multiple (known) use cases, and not "because we can" or "because someone might in some future". In almost every case, those options end to become unused.

../Frenck
Was updating according to your last comment. Are we ready for a review + merge?
Not sure what or how - please assist and/or guide.

Generally speaking, in this PR the delay in reopening the connection is obtained by making slower the closing procedure. This has broken the tests related to the service restart. 
Did you run the test in your environment? 
Did you test the PR in your real installation to see if that sleep is working as you expect?
@crug80 I'm actively using the code. Delaying the closure works for me and in addition catches the errno 111 from pymodbus.

Converted the PR back to draft, as it has failing tests. We cannot action/merge this PR as long as the CI is failing.

../Frenck

This change seems to me too risky by forcing 1 second delay after all the closing procedures. 
if you can, may I suggest to test in your real env the parameter "reconnect_delay" that pymodbus has, but it is not exposed to HA. 
You can do a quick test by adding the following line after the line 270 (after retry_on_empty) of the modbus.py
`"reconnect_delay": 1,`   (increase/decrease).

issue_context.title: Modbus connects too soon after reloading yaml and doesnt evaluate the connection call when it fails
issue_context.body:

The new connection fails but Modbus keeps trying to read values. Reloading the yaml files once again then succeeds. Are you sure that those lines (314-317) of code are really useful and called? (moreover not tested)
As you can see, modbus raises an exception in case of connection failure and it retries..

The code never throws an exception for me. When you review the logs from the attached issue https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/129940 you can see that pymodbus comes back with Errno 111, however the core modbus.py assumes the connection was established and tries communicating.
Lines 314-317 detects that.
